raw_case_text:
The 23-year-old primigest mother had no pregnancy-related complications. Prenatal care was done regularly at a private clinic with unremarkable serology in the first semester: Hepatitis B, HIV, and syphilis negative. She had flu-like syndrome and an episode of fever (38.5 C) 2 days prior to admission. At arrival, she was afebrile and COVID-19 rapid antigen test was negative. She was admitted for unspecified sepsis during labor and treated with ampicillin for 5 days. During her stay, the initial investigation demonstrated an isolated elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) of 130 mg/L. Complete blood count (CBC) was normal, with leucocytes 4.4 x 109/L, platelets 223 x 109/L, and hemoglobin 115 g/L. Urine examination was normal, and hemoculture later was proven negative. Dengue serology was negative. Few hours after admission, the delivery was spontaneous and uneventful.
At Special Care Nursery, the infant was active and pink, with good sucking. The physical examination was unremarkable. Due to the possible risks of perinatal infection, a septic workup was done and showed a normal leucocyte count (11.4 x 109/L), with an absolute neutrophil count of 7.2 x 109/L, lymphocytes of 2.3 x 109/L (20%) and immature to total neutrophil ratio (I/T ratio) 0.01; hemoglobin and platelets were within the normal range (Table 1). Inflammatory markers, however, were elevated: CRP of 34.64 mg/L and procalcitonin (PCT) of 1.48 mcg/L. Per unit protocol for suspected early-onset sepsis, empiric antibiotics including Ampicillin and Cefotaxime were initiated.
At Day 3 of life, the infant started to develop morbilliform rash with petechiae, predominantly found over the back (Figure 1), and intermittent nocturnal fever (38 C). Vital signs were stable. There were neither neurological signs nor hepatosplenomegaly. No mosquito bite marks were reported. Control blood tests showed decreased platelets (78 x 109/L) and increased CRP (43 mg/L). Syphilis tests were nonreactive. Hemoculture and gastric aspirate done at admission were negative. Brain ultrasound, done before Lumbar Puncture (LP), showed no bleeding signs. Heart ultrasound showed no defect. The second blood culture was drawn, and LP was done, with normal results: leucocytes 06/mm3, albumin 0.5 g/L, and glucose 0.79 g/L. Based upon local guidelines, the clinicians upgraded the antibiotics to second line: Meropenem and Amikacin.
About 48 h later, because of the persistently on-off fever and progressively decreasing platelets, we interviewed parents by phone during the restricted period amid COVID pandemic to get more detailed information before any further investigations. According to the mother about 2 days after delivery, she started developing rash, with low-grade fever and persistent arthralgia. Given the information, we decided to rule out other mosquito-borne congenital infections, in an early stage, by combined PCR, which later confirmed the diagnosis of congenital chikungunya (Table 2).
Early-onset neonatal sepsis, culture not proven
Hypoproliferative thrombocytopenia, associated with small-for-gestational-age neonates
Mosquito-borne congenital infection such as congenital dengue
The treatment was supportive. Apyrexia was noted on day 6 of life. Antibiotics were discontinued 7 days after the negativation of the second blood culture. Platelets increased progressively to 112 x 109/L at the discharge (Day 10). She was brought for a follow-up on day 20, with good weight gain and normalized platelets. The girl will be follow up every 3 months until the age of 2 years, following our local follow-up program for low birth weight.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 3-day-old female neonate in the Special Care Nursery developed a morbilliform petechial rash over the back, intermittent nocturnal fever (38 C), and progressive thrombocytopenia following maternal peripartum febrile illness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The neonate was born via spontaneous, uneventful vaginal delivery to a 23-year-old primigravida who had experienced a flu-like syndrome and fever (38.5 C) 2 days prior to admission and was treated peripartum for suspected sepsis with elevated CRP (130 mg/L), negative COVID-19 rapid antigen, negative dengue serology, and negative blood/urine cultures. At birth, the infant was admitted to the Special Care Nursery for perinatal sepsis risk evaluation; she was initially clinically well on empiric ampicillin and cefotaxime (started for elevated neonatal CRP 34.64 mg/L and procalcitonin 1.48 mcg/L). On day 3 of life, the infant developed a morbilliform rash with petechiae predominantly over the back and intermittent nocturnal fevers (38 C). Follow-up phone interview with the parents 48 hours later revealed that the mother had developed a rash, low-grade fever, and persistent arthralgia 2 days postpartum.
subjective.past_medical_history: Small-for-gestational-age / low-birth-weight female neonate born to a 23-year-old primigravida with unremarkable first-trimester prenatal serologies (hepatitis B, HIV, and syphilis negative), maternal fever (38.5 C) 2 days before delivery, and maternal postpartum rash, fever, and persistent arthralgia starting 2 days after delivery.
subjective.review_of_systems: Neonatal review positive for intermittent nocturnal fever (38 C) and morbilliform/petechial truncal rash starting on day 3 of life; good sucking and activity at birth.

objective.physical_examination: At birth: active, pink neonate with good sucking and unremarkable systemic physical examination. On day 3 of life: morbilliform rash with petechiae predominantly over the back and intermittent nocturnal fever (38 C); vital signs remained stable, with no neurological abnormalities, no hepatosplenomegaly, and no mosquito bite marks.
objective.routine_investigations: Maternal peripartum labs: CRP 130 mg/L, WBC 4.4 x 10^9/L, platelets 223 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin 115 g/L, normal urinalysis, and negative COVID-19 rapid antigen, dengue serology, and blood cultures. Neonatal day 1 septic workup: WBC 11.4 x 10^9/L, absolute neutrophil count 7.2 x 10^9/L, lymphocytes 2.3 x 10^9/L (20%), immature-to-total neutrophil (I/T) ratio 0.01, normal hemoglobin and platelets, elevated CRP 34.64 mg/L, and elevated procalcitonin 1.48 mcg/L; admission blood culture and gastric aspirate negative. Neonatal day 3 labs: thrombocytopenia with platelets dropping to 78 x 10^9/L, rising CRP to 43 mg/L, nonreactive syphilis serology, and negative repeat blood culture. Cranial ultrasound: no intracranial hemorrhage. Echocardiogram (heart ultrasound): no structural defect.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture / CSF analysis (day 3 of life): normal with leukocytes 6/mm3, albumin 0.5 g/L, and glucose 0.79 g/L. Combined arboviral RT-PCR panel (performed after maternal postpartum arthralgia/rash history was obtained): positive for chikungunya virus.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Congenital/perinatal chikungunya infection transmitted via maternal peripartum viremia. Early-onset bacterial neonatal sepsis, congenital syphilis, COVID-19, and congenital dengue were excluded. Confirmation: Positive combined RT-PCR for chikungunya virus in the neonate coupled with maternal peripartum fever and postpartum polyarthralgia/rash. Management and outcome: Treated initially with empiric ampicillin and cefotaxime (escalated on day 3 to meropenem and amikacin before bacterial cultures returned negative and antibiotics were discontinued after 7 days), alongside supportive care. The neonate became afebrile on day 6 of life, platelet counts recovered to 112 x 10^9/L at discharge on day 10, and at day-20 follow-up she demonstrated good weight gain and normalized platelets, with scheduled 3-monthly follow-up through age 2 years.
